global.concept_prompt:
Ultra-realistic, cinematic, faceless short-form video that takes the viewer on a single continuous first-person journey: a panicked sprint to and through the door of a modest, mysterious structure in a dramatic remote place, an IMMEDIATE descent down a staircase right inside the door, and a calm off-POV reveal of a hidden, secret, luxurious living space at the bottom.

The video must be composed for a vertical 9:16 frame and must always remain upright, never sideways or horizontal.

The video ALWAYS follows the same fixed five-beat format — only the setting, the structure, and the hidden interior change between episodes:
1. FIRST-PERSON POV at FULL-TILT SPRINT — the lone traveler runs STRAIGHT AT the structure's entrance DOOR, THROWS THE DOOR OPEN WITH HIS HAND, and IMMEDIATELY BEGINS DESCENDING the staircase right inside — all in ONE continuous motion with NO pause at the top of the stairs. The video opens already in full-tilt motion: K0 has the DOOR AT 20–25 METRES AHEAD, CENTERED IN THE FRAME. The world RUSHES PAST at sprint speed (~6–7 m/s). EXTREME body-cam vibration (head bob, strap wobble, gear bouncing, lateral shifts, sharp judders, irregular stumble-recovers, no two consecutive frames alike, camera in all axes). Water droplets streak the lens in wet settings (dust/lens flare in dry). AT THE FINAL MOMENTS, his HAND thrusts forward into the bottom-center of the frame (palm out) and SHOVES the door open INWARD; the door YIELDS INWARD INSTANTLY; the CAMERA PASSES THROUGH the doorway in CONTINUOUS FORWARD MOTION (no recoil, no pushed-back, no bouncing); and WITHOUT BREAKING STRIDE, WITHOUT PAUSING, WITHOUT BREATHING-BREAK, the runner immediately steps onto the FIRST step of the descending staircase that is right inside the doorway. By the end of scene 1 (K1) the camera has ALREADY STEPPED ONTO THE FIRST 1–2 STEPS of the descent, mid-step, body in CONTINUOUS FORWARD-AND-DOWNWARD motion, camera angled DOWNWARD at the remaining descending steps below. K1 is a moment of DOWNWARD MOTION, not a static arrival — there is NO stationary 'arrived at top of stairs, catching breath' moment.
2. FIRST-PERSON POV — CONTINUOUS DESCENT, first half. The runner continues walking DOWN the straight step staircase from the first few steps to mid-descent. REAL WALKING-DOWN-STAIRS BIOMECHANICS: each step is a discrete footfall — the foot lifts off the current step, swings forward, and lands on the next-lower step with a clear downward impact; the camera DIPS DOWN with each footfall and SETTLES briefly before the next step; alternating feet visible in the per-step bob rhythm; cadence approximately 1.5–2 steps per second (controlled walking descent, not sprinting, not floating). Camera angled DOWNWARD throughout. The hand may briefly touch the side-wall railing for balance. THE FOOTSTEPS ON THE STAIRS ARE PROMINENTLY AUDIBLE — each step creates a clear, distinct sound on the SPECIFIC stair material (timber creak / concrete thud / stone tap) that DOMINATES the audio. NEVER a smooth slide down, NEVER feet floating, NEVER stairs scrolling past without footfall. By the end of scene 2 (K2) the camera is at the MIDDLE of the staircase, mid-step, with more descending steps below.
3. FIRST-PERSON POV — CONTINUOUS DESCENT, second half + arrival at the bottom. The runner continues walking DOWN from mid-descent to the bottom. Same REAL WALKING-DOWN-STAIRS BIOMECHANICS, same per-step bob and settle, same PROMINENTLY AUDIBLE footsteps. As the camera reaches the bottom step and STEPS OFF onto the lower-room floor, the camera angle transitions from looking-down-at-steps to LEVEL — looking AHEAD into the lower room. By the end of scene 3 (K3) the camera is at the FLOOR LEVEL of the LOWER ROOM (the hidden luxurious interior), camera LEVEL looking AHEAD into the warm luxury space — the LOWER ROOM INTERIOR (warm furnishings, dramatic luxury) DOMINATES the frame.
4. OFF-POV (third-person) FIRST REVEAL of the hidden luxurious interior. The camera switches to off-POV positioned IN THE LOWER ROOM, looking across the room. The traveler — seen only from behind or in profile, face NEVER shown, clothing/body LOCKED — has just emerged from the staircase and is walking calmly in ONE consistent forward direction across the room, unbothered. The camera slowly TRACKS LATERALLY. The staircase entrance is a SUBTLE, SECONDARY element at ONE edge of the frame.
5. OFF-POV (third-person) HOUSE-TOUR — the traveler walks toward and through an open archway into ANOTHER luxurious room of the hidden residence. The camera follows him from behind in one smooth continuous house-tour move. His clothing, body, silhouette, and gait are IDENTICAL to scene 4.

CAMERA: Scenes 1–3 are real FIRST-PERSON POV — a battered body-cam strapped to the traveler's chest. Scene 1 is EXTREME body-cam vibration ending with the camera ALREADY descending the first steps (no pause at top). Scenes 2 and 3 are POV descent (camera angled DOWN, per-step bob, real walking-down-stairs biomechanics). Scenes 4–5 are calm off-POV third-person. The POV-to-off-POV transition happens cleanly between scenes 3 and 4.

RUNNING & MOVEMENT MUST LOOK REAL — highest priority. In scene 1 the camera must JOLT EXTREMELY DOWN-UP and side-to-side with EACH footfall in a FAST sprint cadence (about 3–4 strides per second). EXTREME body-cam vibration: head bob synced to footfalls; secondary motion from body-cam strap wobble and gear bouncing; lateral camera shifts as the runner weaves around obstacles; sharp judders from hard footfalls on uneven terrain; irregular stumble-recovers; NO TWO CONSECUTIVE FRAMES ARE ALIKE; the camera is constantly moving in all axes (vertical, lateral, rotational). Frame rotates 8–15 degrees per stride. Motion blur at frame edges. Water droplets / lens splash / motion blur (wet settings) or dust / lens flare (dry). Natural raw amateur footage texture like real foot-pursuit body-cam, chaotic and jolting, NOT cinematic. The WORLD RUSHES PAST at real sprint speed — ground FLIES past beneath, terrain at the edges RACES past as a blur. Per-stride SURGE-AND-SETTLE: camera LURCHES FORWARD as the foot pushes off, briefly floats during airborne phase, JOLTS DOWN HARD as the next foot lands. Panicked panting breath. Forearms OCCASIONALLY at the bottom edge of the frame — brief, natural, NOT exaggerated. Door REMAINS the dominant focal point with brief 1–2 shoulder-glances. The MOMENTUM CARRIES STRAIGHT INTO THE DESCENT — there is NO pause at the doorway, NO pause at the top of the stairs, NO breathing break, NO standing-still moment.

DOOR ACTION (scene 1, end of running phase) — HAND OPENS + CAMERA PASSES THROUGH + IMMEDIATELY DESCENDS: the door does NOT open by itself. The runner's HAND thrusts forward into the bottom-center of the frame (palm out, fingers extended, VISIBLY entering frame) and SHOVES the door open INWARD in one fast continuous motion. The door YIELDS INWARD INSTANTLY (swings AWAY from the camera INTO the structure) under the hand's push. The CAMERA PASSES THROUGH the doorway in CONTINUOUS FORWARD MOTION — NO recoil, NO 'pushed-back' effect, NO bouncing off the door. The runner continues forward WITHOUT BREAKING STRIDE and IMMEDIATELY STEPS ONTO THE FIRST STEP of the descending staircase that is right inside. There is NO pause between passing through the doorway and starting the descent. The door NEVER opens outward, NEVER opens slowly, NEVER opens by itself.

STRUCTURE LAYOUT — STAIRS RIGHT INSIDE THE DOOR: the modest structure is essentially a tiny landing at the very TOP of a descending staircase — when the front door opens, the staircase going DOWN is RIGHT THERE. The door opens directly onto the top of the staircase. There is NO interior room, NO foyer, NO hallway. The runner barges through the doorway and immediately starts descending.

THE DESCENT IS ALWAYS A NORMAL STRAIGHT STEP STAIRCASE going DOWN, structurally attached, never floating. NEVER a ladder, vertical ladder, rungs, spiral staircase, circular staircase, ship's ladder, rope ladder, or trapdoor with a ladder. NEVER stairs going up. The traveler only ever descends.

DESCENT DIRECTION — CRITICAL: K1 = camera already descending the first 1–2 steps, mid-step, body in motion downward, angled DOWN at remaining steps below. K2 = mid-descent, still angled DOWN, several more steps below. K3 = at the bottom, camera LEVEL with the lower-room floor, looking AHEAD into the warm luxury interior. NEVER ascending. NEVER stationary at top.

DESCENT BIOMECHANICS (scenes 2 and 3) — REAL WALKING-DOWN-STAIRS: each step is a discrete footfall — foot lifts off current step, swings forward, lands on next-lower step with a brief downward impact; camera DIPS DOWN with each footfall and SETTLES briefly before the next; ~1.5–2 steps per second cadence; alternating feet visible in the per-step bob rhythm; the hand may briefly touch the side-wall railing for balance. NEVER a smooth slide, NEVER floating, NEVER stairs scrolling past without footfall, NEVER gliding down, NEVER feet not visibly stepping.

INTERIOR CONSISTENCY (scenes 4 and 5) — across K4 and K5 the hidden interior must be PERFECTLY CONSISTENT. Same walls, ceiling, floor, furniture, lighting, palette, and materials in every frame. The lone traveler has IDENTICAL clothing, body, hair/hood, height, gait, and silhouette. He walks in ONE consistent forward direction per clip.

The payoff, every episode, is the hidden, secret, LUXURIOUS, fully-furnished LIVING space below. The lower-room interior must look DISTINCTLY different from the modest exterior/entrance landing — warm, luxurious, dramatic — to make the descent feel meaningful.

Everything must look like something a real, wealthy, eccentric person could genuinely have built and could genuinely own — human-scale, physically plausible, photoreal.

The audio is ONLY real, natural, diegetic sound that matches exactly what is on screen. NEVER any music. EVERY kling_prompt must explicitly state 'no music' AND name the SPECIFIC surface material for footsteps. Scenes 2 AND 3 (the descent) MUST describe the footsteps on the SPECIFIC stair material as PROMINENT, CLEARLY AUDIBLE, DOMINANT — each step a distinct sound.

No frame may ever contain words, numbers, subtitles, captions, logos, watermarks, or UI. This channel uses NO on-screen text of any kind.
